A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TOF is a rare but potentially associated with PITX2 deletion.
PITX2 is a gene that is associated with a variety of clinical manifestations, including ocular, dental, and cardiac anomalies.

TOF is not a feature of the Axenfeld Rieger Syndrome, and that the deletion of PITX 2 is a cause of TOF, but that the phenotype of the patient with a PITX 2 deletion is not the same as the phenotype of the ARS patients.

a 4q25 deletion can cause an ocular malformation syndrome without ocular features.
